children: As artificial intelligence rapidly changes how software is built, businesses operate and workers acquire new skills, Andreessen Horowitz is betting that the traditional four-year college model may not be the only route into the technology industry.

The venture capital firm is incubating the Horowitz Andreessen Academy, a full-time, in-person school in San Francisco designed for students coming out of high school and built around AI, hands-on work and direct access to the tech industry.

The Academy will combine coursework with company placements and student-led projects. Its co-op program will allow students to work during the academic year, rather than limiting industry experience to summer internships.

Founding partners include Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit and Stripe, potentially giving students exposure to companies at the center of the current AI and technology boom.

AI sits at the center of the Academy's curriculum, reflecting the growing importance of the technology across the economy. Courses will include Frontier Systems, AI Inference Engineering, the modern software developer and the history of digital computing.

The school says students will work on challenges that either require AI to solve or involve creating problems that current AI systems cannot yet solve. Classes will be taught by technology founders, investors and other industry leaders.

Technology executives including NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi and Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison are expected to visit the campus and speak with students.

The launch comes as AI is increasingly becoming part of the way people learn, code and work, raising questions about which skills traditional education should prioritize. Rather than treating AI as another subject, the Academy is building its educational model around the technology and the industries developing it.

title: Andreessen Horowitz launches AI school for students who skip college
